input.quote: 9.8 Any Party shall have the right to review or audit the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9. In affording the right to review or audit, any such Party whose records are being reviewed or audited shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit.
input.rationale: Subparagraph 9.8 is the only audit right that binds us as an audited Party (Subparagraph 9.4 and 4.7 run against the Supplier, and 10.8 is an inspection right exercisable by each Party at its own expense, which also benefits us). Although reciprocal, 9.8 lets any other APCN 2 Party review or audit our cost books with no frequency limit and no notice requirement, which is walk-away territory (unlimited and unannounced audits); the only control is that the right is exercised through the F&ASC's audit procedures (9.9), which are outside the Agreement and do not set frequency or notice. Cost allocation already sits at or above the fallback, because the audited Party recovers its entire reasonable compliance costs from the requesting Party with no underpayment threshold, so we left that mechanic untouched. Our edit adds only the fallback once-per-year cap and 15 days' notice; we did not press the preferred 30-day/independent-auditor/off-site package for this reciprocal cost-verification regime.

ops.oldText: Any Party shall have the right to review or audit the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9.
ops.newText: Any Party shall have the right, no more than once per year and on 15 days' notice, to review or audit the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a once-per-year cap and 15 days' notice to the review/audit right in Subparagraph 9.8, since it is otherwise unlimited and unannounced; the existing cost-recovery mechanic already puts audit costs on the requesting Party, so we left it unchanged.
proposal.summary: Add once-per-year frequency limit and 15 days' notice to the Paragraph 9.8 review/audit right

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
mappings.quote: In affording the right to review or audit, any such Party whose records are being reviewed or audited shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit.
